title: See-saw extends a prescribed section isomorphism uniquely
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $V$ be a proper geometrically integral $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], let $x\in V(k)$ [def-pc-rational-point], and let $T$ be a smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $q:V\times_kT\to T$ and $s_x:T\to V\times_kT$ be the projection and the section $t\mapsto(x,t)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-rational-point]. Let $\mathcal E,\mathcal F$ be invertible sheaves on $V\times_kT$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose that for every $t\in T(k)$ the restrictions $\mathcal E_t$ and $\mathcal F_t$ to $V\times_k\{t\}$ are isomorphic. Then every isomorphism
$$\alpha:s_x^*\mathcal E\xrightarrow{\sim}s_x^*\mathcal F$$
extends uniquely to an isomorphism $\widetilde\alpha:\mathcal E\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$ satisfying $s_x^*\widetilde\alpha=\alpha$. In particular, if an invertible sheaf $\mathcal H$ on $V\times_kT$ is trivial on every such fibre, then $\mathcal H\cong q^*s_x^*\mathcal H$. All restrictions are tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 5.16 and Corollaries 5.17–5.18, printed p.26, with the evaluation construction of the isomorphism in the proof of 5.16. The section prescribes the base-factor isomorphism; uniqueness uses proper geometric integrality (global functions are constants). T is explicitly smooth, hence reduced: this is not a claim over arbitrary nonreduced bases.

proof.text: Put $X=V\times_kT$. The structure morphism of $V$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field], proper by hypothesis, and locally of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth], since a field is Noetherian and proper includes finite type. It is quasi-compact and separated, hence of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] to this scheme morphism and base change to $T$: $q$ is proper, flat and of finite presentation. Its fibre over $t$ is $V_{\kappa(t)}$, geometrically integral by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and $s_x$ is a section. Apply [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: its unique fibre is $T$, so $T$ is reduced. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], hence locally Noetherian. These are the base hypotheses needed for Grauert, including the locally Noetherian hypothesis in clause (4) of its current blueprint statement.

Set $\mathcal H=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal E^\vee$. By [def-sc-invertible-module], local bases of $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal F$ identify $\mathcal H$ with $\mathcal O_X$; its dual is the inverse line bundle. The tensor-pullback formula [def-pc-module-pullback] gives $\mathcal H_t=\mathcal F_t\otimes\mathcal E_t^\vee$. The given fibre isomorphism therefore makes $\mathcal H_t$ trivial at every $k$-rational point of $T$. The prescribed $\alpha$ corresponds, in these same rank-one bases, to an isomorphism $a:\mathcal O_T\xrightarrow{\sim}s_x^*\mathcal H$; this correspondence sends a scalar matrix to its section of $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal E^\vee$.

source.place: I Corollary 5.17, tensor by the inverse bundle

proof.text: Every closed point of $T$ is $k$-rational by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], so the preceding triviality holds at every closed point. Apply [lem-sc-picard-fiber-triviality-closed] to $q,\mathcal H,s_x$: its hypotheses were checked in step 1. The set $Z$ of points with trivial residue-field fibre is closed. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], the closed points of $T$ are dense in $T$ (take its closed subset to be $T$). Since they all lie in $Z$, $Z=T$. Thus $\mathcal H_t$ is trivial for every scheme point $t$, not just the originally prescribed rational points.

For each $t$, [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety](2) applied over $\kappa(t)$ gives $H^0(V_{\kappa(t)},\mathcal O)=\kappa(t)$: properness follows by base change as in step 1, and geometric integrality is preserved by further field extension by its definition. Since $\mathcal H_t$ is trivial, $h^0(X_t,\mathcal H_t)=1$ everywhere. The module $\mathcal H$ is of finite presentation and flat over $T$: on a trivializing open its stalk is one copy of $\mathcal O_{X,z}$, which is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,q(z)}$ since $q$ is flat. Apply [thm-pc-semicontinuity-base-change] with $q=0$. Its reducedness and local Noetherian hypotheses hold by step 1, and the dimension function is constant, including on every generization. Consequently $N=q_*\mathcal H$ is finite locally free and the canonical maps $N\otimes\kappa(t)\to H^0(X_t,\mathcal H_t)$ are isomorphisms. Their targets have dimension one, so every local free rank of $N$ is one: $N$ is invertible.

source.place: I 5.15 and proof of 5.16, first paragraph

proof.text: Take the adjunction evaluation $e:q^*N\to\mathcal H$ from [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. For an open $U\subseteq T$, a section $m\in N(U)=\mathcal H(q^{-1}U)$ and a local function $b$ on $q^{-1}U$, the map is $b\otimes m\mapsto bm$. Hence its restriction to $X_t$, using the canonical base-change map of step 4, is exactly $\mathcal O_{X_t}\otimes_{\kappa(t)}H^0(X_t,\mathcal H_t)\to\mathcal H_t$, $b\otimes m\mapsto bm$. In any chosen trivialization of $\mathcal H_t$, constants are all its global sections by step 4, so this is the multiplication isomorphism $\mathcal O_{X_t}\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(t)\to\mathcal O_{X_t}$. Thus $e$ is an isomorphism on every residue-field fibre at every point of $X$: first restrict to $X_{q(z)}$, then to $\kappa(z)$. Both its source and target are locally free of rank one. Apply [lem-sc-finite-locally-free-residue-isomorphism] on $X$ to conclude that $e$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: I 5.10–5.11 and proof of 5.16, evaluation paragraph

proof.text: Pull $e$ back along $s_x$, identifying $s_x^*q^*N=N$ by $qs_x=\mathrm{id}_T$ and [def-pc-module-pullback]; write $b:N\xrightarrow{\sim}s_x^*\mathcal H$ for the resulting isomorphism. Then $c=b^{-1}a:\mathcal O_T\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ defines $h=e\circ q^*c:\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H$. Its section restriction is $s_x^*h=b c=a$. In local rank-one bases the corresponding morphism $\widetilde\alpha:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$ is multiplication by the same unit as $h$. These local maps glue, since $\mathcal H=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal E^\vee$; their local inverses glue too. Thus $\widetilde\alpha$ is an isomorphism and $s_x^*\widetilde\alpha=\alpha$.

source.place: I 5.18, section restriction, with explicit prescribed-isomorphism normalization

proof.text: For uniqueness, first compute functions on $X$. By [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety](2), $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)=k$. For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$, $A$ is flat over the field $k$ by [lem-pc-flat-field]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-stein-flat-base-change-global-sections] identifies the canonical pullback $A\to\Gamma(V\times_kU,\mathcal O)$ with $k\otimes_k A\to\Gamma(V\times_kU,\mathcal O)$ and makes it bijective. For a global function $u$ on $X$, each restriction over $U$ consequently equals $q^*v_U$ for a unique $v_U\in A$. Applying $s_x^*$ shows $v_U=(s_x^*u)|_U$, so these local equalities give $u=q^*s_x^*u$. An automorphism of the invertible module $\mathcal E$ is multiplication by a unique global unit $u$: on trivializing opens it is a unit scalar, and these scalars agree on overlaps because conjugating a rank-one scalar by a change of basis leaves it unchanged [def-sc-invertible-module]. The ratio of two extensions of $\alpha$ is such an automorphism, with $s_x^*u=1$. The function identity just proved gives $u=q^*1=1$. The extensions are therefore equal.

Finally let $\mathcal H$ be as in the last assertion. On each fibre, $q^*s_x^*\mathcal H$ is the tensor product of $\mathcal O_{V}$ with the one-dimensional fibre of $s_x^*\mathcal H$, hence is trivial. Apply the extension assertion with $\mathcal E=q^*s_x^*\mathcal H$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal H$ and the canonical identity $s_x^*q^*s_x^*\mathcal H\cong s_x^*\mathcal H$. It yields $q^*s_x^*\mathcal H\cong\mathcal H$; invert it for the stated orientation. If $T$ is empty all module maps are uniquely determined, so the same conclusion holds without a nonemptiness assumption.

lean.statement: theorem rigidified_product_seesaw {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {V T : Scheme.{u}} (f : V ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : T ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] [GeometricallyIntegral f] [Smooth g] [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g] (x : f.fieldPoints k) : (∀ (E F : (Limits.pullback f g).Modules) [E.IsInvertible] [F.IsInvertible], (∀ t : g.fieldPoints k, Nonempty ((tensorPullback (Limits.pullback.fst (Limits.pullback.snd f g) t.1)).obj E ≅ (tensorPullback (Limits.pullback.fst (Limits.pullback.snd f g) t.1)).obj F)) → ∀ α : (tensorPullback (f.fieldPointBaseChange x (Over.mk g))).obj E ≅ (tensorPullback (f.fieldPointBaseChange x (Over.mk g))).obj F, ∃! e : E ≅ F, (tensorPullback (f.fieldPointBaseChange x (Over.mk g))).mapIso e = α) ∧ (∀ (H : (Limits.pullback f g).Modules) [H.IsInvertible], (∀ t : g.fieldPoints k, Nonempty ((tensorPullback (Limits.pullback.fst (Limits.pullback.snd f g) t.1)).obj H ≅ SheafOfModules.unit _)) → Nonempty (H ≅ (tensorPullback (Limits.pullback.snd f g)).obj ((tensorPullback (f.fieldPointBaseChange x (Over.mk g))).obj H)))
